title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يحاضر عن أمة الجسد الواحد
title_en: The Sheikh Lectures on 'The Community of a Single Body'
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو حفظه الله تعالى مساء اليوم الخميس 11-09-2014 محاضرة بعنوان: " أمة الجسد الواحد " تحدث فيها فضيلته عن عظمة هذه الأمة و أن الله تعالى شرفها و هداها وميزها واختصها على غيرها من سائر الأمم بكرامات كثيرة في الدنيا من أبرزها أنه مَنً عليهم ببعثة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي هو خير خلق الله و اتقاهم و أحبهم إليه فقد قال الله تعالى : (لقد من الله على المؤمنين إذ بعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم ) كما تحدث الشيخ عن فضل يوم الجمعة الذي شرف الله به هذه الأمة و جعله يوم عيد لهم بعد أن أضل عنه اليهود والنصارى، مستدلا بحديث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم " نحن الآخرون السابقون يوم القيامة، بيد أنهم أوتوا الكتاب من قبلنا، وأوتيناه من بعدهم، ثم هذا يومهم الذي فرض عليهم - يعني الجمعة - فاختلفوا فيه ، فهدانا الله له ، والناس لنا فيه تبع ، اليهود غدا ، والنصارى بعد غد " . كما تحدث فضيلته عن وجوب نصرة المسلمين المضطهدين في كافة أنحاء العالم بالمال و الدعاء، مبينا أن الله تعالى جعل نصرة المسلمين واجبا شرعيا إن هم استنصرونا في الدين و قد فعلوا، فواجب علينا في حقهم الدعاء و التبرع لهم فلا يتم إيمان أحدكم حتى يحب لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) delivered this evening, Thursday 11-09-2014, a lecture entitled 'The Community of a Single Body', in which he spoke of the greatness of this community, and of how God the Exalted has honoured it, guided it, marked it out and singled it out above all other communities with many honours in this world — the most prominent of them being that He bestowed His favour upon them in the sending of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), who is the best of God's creation, the most God-conscious of them and the most beloved to Him; for God the Exalted said: {God indeed bestowed favour upon the believers when He raised up among them a Messenger from among themselves} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:164).

The Sheikh also spoke of the merit of Friday, by which God honoured this community and which He made a day of festival for them, after He had let the Jews and the Christians stray from it, adducing as evidence the hadith of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "We are the last, the foremost on the Day of Resurrection — save that they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. Then this is their day which was made obligatory upon them" — that is, Friday — "and they differed over it; and God guided us to it. The people follow us in it: the Jews tomorrow, and the Christians the day after tomorrow."

His Eminence also spoke of the obligation to support persecuted Muslims in every part of the world with money and with supplication, explaining that God the Exalted made the support of Muslims an obligation in the Sharia if they seek our support in the matter of religion — and they have done so; so it is obligatory upon us, in their regard, to supplicate for them and to donate to them, for the faith of any one of you is not complete until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.

flags.arabic: بعد أن أضل عنه اليهود والنصارى
options: after He had let the Jews and the Christians stray from it (subject: God, matching فهدانا الله له in the hadith)
after the Jews and the Christians had strayed from it
after they had been led astray from it
flags.note: The subject of أضل is unmarked in the Arabic. The pairing with هدى in the hadith the Sheikh then quotes points to God as the subject, which is the first reading. The second makes the two communities the agents of their own error and is a materially different theological claim. Recorded rather than resolved; the English takes the first reading because the hadith supplies it.

flags.arabic: أضل عنه اليهود والنصارى … اليهود غدا، والنصارى بعد غد
flags.context: the passage on Friday and the hadith quoted in support
flags.note: EDITORIAL, LOW. The passage and the hadith it quotes speak of Jews and Christians as communities guided away from, or differing over, the day of assembly. The hadith is one of the well-known reports on the merit of Friday; the Sheikh gives no narrator, collection or grading for it and none has been added. Translated exactly and neither softened nor sharpened. Noted because the corpus is being published in English, where a reader meets it without the context a sermon audience has.

flags.arabic: إن هم استنصرونا في الدين و قد فعلوا
flags.context: the ground for the obligation to support persecuted Muslims
options: if they seek our support in the matter of religion — and they have done so
if they call on us for help in religion, as they have
flags.note: The condition is the wording of Sūrat al-Anfāl 8:72 (وإن استنصروكم في الدين فعليكم النصر). The Sheikh does not cite the verse and the English does not supply it in the text. The added clause 'and they have done so' is his own: it converts a conditional obligation into a present one, and must not be dropped.

flags.context: أنه مَنً عليهم ببعثة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): the shadda and vowel are misplaced in the CMS text. Preserved in body_ar.

translator_notes: A news report of a lecture, not a transcript. The two scriptural texts are quoted in the report; everything else is the site's summary.

The closing clause, 'the faith of any one of you is not complete until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself', is a prophetic report used without introduction; the report runs it into the site's own sentence, and the English keeps it there rather than setting it off as a separate quotation, which would attribute to the report a framing it does not have.
The source encloses the Qur'anic text in round brackets; the English uses the corpus convention. Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
